nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used low-order polynomial regression models (linear, quadratic, and cubic) to estimate lifespan trajectories of brain structure volumes. Model selection was performed using Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) after confirming statistical significance via F-statistic (ANOVA) and T-statistic for coefficients. Most selected models were quadratic, with inferior lateral ventricle models being cubic.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To estimate the volume trajectories, we considered several low order polynomial models: Linear model, Quadratic model, Cubic model... As in Coupé et al. (2017, 2019), a polynomial model was considered as a potential candidate only when simultaneously F-statistic based on ANOVA (i.e., model vs. constant model) was found significant (p < .05) and when all its coefficients were also significant using T-statistic (p < .05). Afterwards, to select the most relevant model between these potential candidates, we used the Bayesian Information Criterion

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: MRI-derived structure volumes, including hippocampus/amygdala and inferior lateral ventricle volumes, plus tissue segmentations for GM/WM/CSF.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: After a full screening of the most discriminant structures between AD and normal aging based on MRI volumetric analysis of 3,032 subjects; These structures are combined to create tissue segmentations (gray matter [GM], white matter [WM], and cerebrospinal fluid [CSF]); we decided to combine the volume of hippocampus, amygdala, and inferior lateral ventricle to propose a novel HAVAs.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Coupe2022.pdf.md: Abstract; Coupe2022.pdf.md: 2.2 | Image processing; Coupe2022.pdf.md: 2.5 | Classification using volume trajectories

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative models used age as the sole explanatory variable, with polynomial terms (linear, quadratic, and cubic) fitted to capture non-linear age trajectories across the lifespan. The model form is: volume = β0 + β1*age (linear), + β2*age² (quadratic), + β3*age³ (cubic). ICV was used for volume normalization but not as a predictor in the regression model.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: To create our lifespan models, we estimated normal and pathological trajectories of structure volumes across the entire lifespan... To estimate the volume trajectories, we considered several low order polynomial models: Linear model, Quadratic model [β0 + β1*age + β2*age²], Cubic model [β0 + β1*age + β2*age² + β3*age³]
